evidence.quote: {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:anoyen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|anoyen}}, from {{der|en|fro|enoiier|anoier|t=to bother, disturb}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|inodio|inodiāre|t=to make loathsome}}, derived from {{der|en|la|odium|t=loathing, hatred}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|dreċċan}}, {{m|ang|gremman}}.

"vexed, peeved, offended," late 13c., past-participle adjective from annoy (v.). See origin and meaning of annoyed. from Anglo-French anuier , Old French enoiier "to weary, vex, anger," anuier "be troublesome or irksome to;" according to French sources these are from Late Latin inodiare "make loathsome," from Latin (esse) in odio "(it is to me) hateful," from ablative of odium "hatred," from PIE root *od- (2) "to hate" (see odium ).
